newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore electronics shares ignore US data midday.
newsitem.headline: Singapore electronics shares ignore US data midday.

text.p: Singapore electronic stocks shrugged off U.S. December book-to-bill data finding support on retail bargain-hunting on Friday afternoon, dealers said.
"The outlook for electronics is fairly positive and nobody wanted to be left behind," a local brokerage dealer said, citing good demand for second board issues.
But buying in blue chips was tempered by jitters in Japan -- where the Nikkei index fell more than 800 ponts in afternoon trading -- and ahead of the weekend, traders said.
At the midday break, Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials index was up 4.20 points at 2,257.93.
Brisk turnover of 101.84 million shares was mainly centred on small capitalisation issues.
Electronics continued to attract retail demand on forecasts of improved sales this year despite a lower-than-expected U.S. December semiconductor book-to-bill ratio.
The ratio for December fell to 1.10 compared with November's 1.16.
Gainers included Creative Technology, which rebounded by Singapore $0.50 to $15.40. F.E. Livingston rose $0.30 to $7.30, and SPH Foreign up $0.20 to $28.60.
